items.title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
items.summary: PHP 8.6 introduces stricter default behaviors to reduce potential attack vectors. The update removes permissive settings that previously allowed unsafe code execution.

items.title: Friday Squid Blogging: The Largest Squid Ever Filmed
items.summary: The article documents the filming of the largest squid ever captured near Japan’s Ogasawara Islands in December 2006. It also references unrelated security stories and blog moderation policy.

items.title: Dialing for Data: Inside the Com’s High-Profile Heists
items.summary: Unit 42 analyzes Com affiliate vishing attacks targeting healthcare and finance. The post offers actionable defense guidance against cloud data theft and extortion campaigns.

items.title: West Virginia Legislature hit with cyber incident affecting IT systems
items.summary: A cybersecurity incident disrupted IT systems at the West Virginia Legislature starting Thursday. The disruption was contained and did not spread to other government entities.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
items.summary: Researchers found that stolen Visa and Mastercard data included information useful for phishing but did not contain financial details. The data could aid attackers in credential harvesting.

items.title: China's 'Armory Castle' Lays Siege to VMware vCenter Zero-Day
items.summary: A China‑nexus threat group likely had a VMware vCenter zero‑day ready during the latest major update cycle. The group targeted VMware vCenter to exploit known vulnerabilities.

items.title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
items.summary: Signal criticized Apple, Google, and Microsoft for not providing adequate AI agent controls. The company emphasized protecting user privacy against intrusive AI features.

items.title: US companies’ use of Chinese open weight AI draws rebuke from House chairmen
items.summary: House Homeland Security Committee investigated U.S. companies using low‑cost open‑weight AI models. The inquiry highlighted potential security risks associated with these models.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Signal blocks Apple, Google AI screenshotting in response to ‘existential threat’ to privacy app
items.summary: Signal now blocks screenshots by Apple, Google, and Microsoft AI agents to protect user privacy. The move follows a similar block implemented for Microsoft last year.

items.title: Container Store restores systems after cyberattack
items.summary: The Container Store’s parent company, Neighborhood Intelligence, announced that the retailer restored its website and systems after a weekend cyberattack. The incident was contained with no reported data loss.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: n0n extortion gang leaks data of JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard customers
items.summary: The extortion group n0n breached third‑party service providers for JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard, leaking customer data online. The leak includes personal and financial information of customers of the three major financial firms. The incident highlights the risk of third‑party vulnerabilities.

items.title: Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data
items.summary: Bell Canada confirmed a breach on November 17, 2026 by an 'agentic' threat actor that stole enterprise customer data, including information from a system used to order and provision telecom circuits. The attack targeted internal systems and exposed sensitive customer details. Bell is investigating the scope of the data loss.

items.title: In Security, Words Matter as Much as Tools, Maybe More
items.summary: Cyber leaders emphasize that clear, disciplined communication is a frontline defense in cloud security and AI adoption. The article argues that effective messaging can mitigate risks as much as technical controls. It calls for better communication practices across enterprises.

items.title: WhatsApp Patches 3 Security Flaws, Including Android Bug Suspected of Use in Scams
items.summary: Meta’s WhatsApp fixed three security vulnerabilities, one affecting Android that may have been used in scam messages. The CVE‑2026‑23871 flaw involved incomplete validation of external ad‑reply URLs. The patch addresses the issue in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android.

items.title: Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server
items.summary: Threat actors employed the open‑source AI penetration‑testing framework Cairn to discover a zero‑day vulnerability in a medical imaging application. The vulnerability allowed them to take control of the server. The incident demonstrates the risk of AI tools in adversarial use.

items.title: China attackers deployed AI agents that autonomously found and exploited a 0-day to take over a university server
items.summary: Chinese threat actors used AI agents that adapted for nearly a full day without human input to locate and exploit a zero‑day in a university server. The attack persisted until the vulnerability was discovered. The case shows autonomous AI capabilities in cyber attacks.

items.title: Amazon says Chinese hackers used Cairn AI tool to discover apparent zero-day during attack on university
items.summary: Amazon reported that a China‑linked threat actor used the open‑source AI tool Cairn to attack two universities, potentially discovering a zero‑day bug. The attackers persisted in the attack, exploiting the vulnerability to gain control. The incident highlights the misuse of AI tools for exploitation.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: What We Missed: Nvidia CEO Scandal Rocks AI Industry
items.summary: The video discusses recent news missed by the publication, including the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Microsoft cloud outage. The segment covers industry impacts and reactions. It provides context on recent AI industry developments.

items.title: Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays to Hide Credential Theft and Device Control
items.summary: Researchers identified the Bazuka Android malware framework that uses fake screen overlays to conceal credential theft and remote device control. The malware integrates large language models for victim management. It was discovered during an investigation of an NFC‑relay banking Trojan.

items.title: Dutch data watchdog highlights safety issues with AI glasses
items.summary: The Dutch data protection authority warned that AI glasses misinterpret medication instructions and other scenarios, posing safety risks. The devices could lead to incorrect usage or harm. The watchdog urges caution and further safety testing.

items.title: NSA resumes normal operations following internal network disruptions
items.summary: NSA has resumed normal operations after internal network disruptions. Some facilities remain in Code Orange, delaying openings for non‑essential staff. Employees must check in with supervisors.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: WhatsApp Fixes Flaw Uncovered While Disrupting Scam Campaign
items.summary: WhatsApp discovered and fixed CVE‑2026‑23871, a vulnerability that could have made scam messages more credible. The flaw was identified by WhatsApp’s security team during a scam campaign disruption.

items.title: Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info
items.summary: J.P. Morgan Chase reported a data breach at a third‑party service provider. The breach exposed personal and marketing data of Chase, Visa, and Mastercard customers.

items.title: Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
items.summary: Storing passwords in spreadsheets can hide weak, reused, or compromised credentials. Centralized password management improves visibility, identifies risks, and simplifies secure sharing.

items.title: Cyber Director Cairncross out as White House resets cyber leadership
items.summary: Sean Cairncross is leaving the White House; Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon’s CIO, has been named acting cyber czar.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Dozens of credit unions hit by supplier breach that went unnoticed for six weeks
items.summary: Ireland’s Data Protection Commission received over 40 breach notifications from credit unions that used a Belfast-based data processor; the breach went unnoticed for six weeks.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Ransomware Recovery Takes 20 Days for the Typical Victim, Report Finds
items.summary: A Rubrik report shows ransomware victims recover in a median of 20 days; 28% of cases take longer than six weeks.

items.title: N-able says recent security breach led to major service outage
items.summary: N‑able reported that attackers breached one of its servers, causing a major outage of Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services worldwide.

items.title: VMware vCenter zero-day exploited for months before patch (CVE-2026-123890)
items.summary: A China‑linked group, Armory Castle, exploited VMware vCenter zero‑day CVE‑2026‑123890 from September until a patch was released; the vulnerability has a CVSS score of 9.8.

items.title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑99312 allows a KVM guest on AMD hosts to read up to 127 GB of host memory, potentially exposing other customers; the flaw is fixed in newer kernels.

items.title: UK government can't keep its encryption-busting order to Apple a secret, tribunal rules
items.summary: A UK tribunal ruled that the government cannot keep its encryption‑busting order to Apple secret; the notice can be acknowledged but the demands remain confidential.

items.title: Spy court blasts UK secrecy, forces government to admit Apple ‘backdoor’ demand
items.summary: A UK spy court criticized government secrecy and forced an admission of an Apple backdoor demand. The court noted the notice could be acknowledged without compromising national security, but details remain undisclosed.

items.title: Microsoft now automatically installs Windows 11 26H2 on unmanaged devices
items.summary: Microsoft is automatically upgrading eligible unmanaged devices to Windows 11 26H2 without IT management.

items.title: Opening a 400-Year-Old Cryptex
items.summary: Researchers used CT scanning to recover the code of a 400‑year‑old cryptex padlock; a commercial USB‑drive cryptex is now available for purchase.

items.title: Mail Bombing Attacks Fuel IT Helpdesk Impersonation Scams
items.summary: Researchers uncovered a large‑scale campaign where attackers flood inboxes with emails and then impersonate IT helpdesk staff to gain account access.

items.title: SBC Medical Group Data Breach Impacts Over 2 Million
items.summary: Threat actors accessed databases containing customer information from SBC Medical Group clinics in Japan. Over 2 million individuals were affected.

items.title: JPMorgan Confirms Customer Data Breach Following Third-Party Compromise
items.summary: JPMorgan confirmed a customer data breach after a third‑party compromise. Ransomware actor N0n claimed attacks on JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard, leaking data on its dark‑web site.

items.title: Windows 11 passkey bug cries failure after successful sign-in
items.summary: A Windows 11 passkey bug caused misleading Android error messages after successful sign‑in. An optional update for versions 25H2 and 26H2 addresses the issue.

items.title: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
items.summary: F5 issued emergency patches for five critical BIG‑IP vulnerabilities that could enable denial‑of‑service or remote code execution. Customers are urged to apply the fixes.

items.title: Ruby Patches Ruby2Shell Vulnerability That Could Lead to RCE
items.summary: Ruby patched CVE‑2026‑132825, a heap‑based buffer overflow known as Ruby2Shell that could lead to remote code execution. The update resolves the RCE risk.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network
items.summary: Threat actors exploited Cisco Expressway CVE‑2026‑76466 (CVSS 9.8) to breach a Russian organization. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access the device and internal network.

items.title: Metasploit Wrap Up: Breaking Zimbra's Identity Boundaries
items.summary: Metasploit added a new shared mixin, Msf::Exploit::Remote::HTTP::Zimbra, to its Zimbra modules. The change provides a common foundation for account/admin SOAP authentication and identity resolution.

items.title: 265,000 Oyster photocard customers’ data exposed in Transport for London breach
items.summary: Transport for London warned that account details of approximately 265,000 Oyster photocard holders may have been exposed. The breach was detected on 16 November and the photocard system was taken offline.

items.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day to Gain Admin Access and Steal Data
items.summary: Armory Castle, a China‑linked group, exploited VMware vCenter Server CVE‑2026‑123890 (CVSS 9.8) to bypass authentication and gain administrative access, enabling data theft.

items.title: Windows 11 KB5132057 update released with 28 changes and fixes
items.summary: Microsoft released the Windows 11 KB5132057 preview update, which includes 28 changes. Improvements cover Windows Search, Windows Hello, and the Run dialog.

items.title: N-able Blames Service Disruption on Cyberattack
items.summary: N‑Able attributes a service outage affecting Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud to a cyberattack that could have led to credential theft.

items.title: Suspected North Korea-Aligned Group Hides C2 on Solana Blockchain
items.summary: Cisco Talos links a RAT that uses the Solana blockchain for command and control and can survive Windows resets to the UAT‑12643 threat group.

items.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Cite Third-Party Incidents Amid Data Leak
items.summary: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard blame a data leak on third‑party providers after the N0n extortion group released customer data.

items.title: ROMULUS ClickFix Attacks Deliver RAT That Can Spy on Users and Control PCs
items.summary: Threat actors use ROMULUS ClickFix to deliver a remote access trojan similar to CNCMachineRMS, enabling spying and remote control of PCs.

items.title: It’s time to retire vanity security dashboards
items.summary: Estée Lauder’s OT Security Architect argues that vanity dashboards generate repetitive alerts that waste analyst time and mask underlying problems in manufacturing environments.

items.title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It
items.summary: FastUnlock is a zero‑day that lets physical attackers run programs on a locked Windows PC without signing in, granting only limited account access.

items.title: Most CIOs and CISOs expect to contain attacks, though few can reach their gear right away
items.summary: A survey of 514 CIOs and CISOs shows most cannot quickly access critical network infrastructure during outages, creating a gap during ransomware or update incidents.

items.title: Flaws in VMware and KVM need attention, if you have time while fixing Java, PHP, and everything else
items.summary: Critical Virtzilla bugs in VMware and KVM allow authentication bypass, prompting Digital Ocean to address the issue amid other security fixes.

items.title: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
items.summary: Broadcom released security updates for a VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass that Chinese‑linked hackers have used in zero‑day attacks since September 2026.

items.title: Germ Network infects Android, but in a good way
items.summary: Bluesky’s encrypted messaging app for Android supports multiple identities without requiring a phone number, allowing users to create separate profiles.

items.title: Android developer verification will reach every install source, with a side door for power users
items.summary: Google will enforce developer verification on all Android install sources worldwide from January 2027, restricting unverified apps on certified devices; the rollout starts with seven major app distributors.

items.title: Hackers steal data of 1.6 million SBC Medical Group customers
items.summary: SBC Medical Group disclosed that two cybersecurity incidents exposed personal data of 1.6 million customers and employees, prompting a filing with the SEC.

items.title: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express
items.summary: ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 to patch three critical vulnerabilities that could let remote attackers gain administrative control of the console and managed devices.

items.title: Chase, Visa, Mastercard confirm third-party cyberattacks that may have exposed customers' info
items.summary: Chase, Visa, and Mastercard confirmed third‑party cyberattacks that potentially exposed customer information following earlier service outages.

items.title: CVE-2026-123890: Critical Authentication Bypass in VMware vCenter
items.summary: Broadcom issued a critical advisory for CVE‑2026‑123890, an authentication bypass in VMware vCenter’s Directory Service, with a CVSS score of 9.8.

items.title: Second Norwegian Energy Company Breached in Two Days
items.summary: A second Norwegian energy company suffered a breach within two days of the first incident, though no connection between the attacks has been established.

items.title: Critical PHP Flaws Allow Code Execution, But Don't Panic 'PHP2Shell'-Style
items.summary: Seven critical PHP flaws that could enable code execution were patched in November’s release, though exploitability depends on configuration.

items.title: Newly Patched VMware vCenter Flaw Exploited as Zero-Day by Chinese APT
items.summary: A China‑linked APT group exploited a VMware vCenter authentication bypass as a zero‑day before Broadcom released a patch, according to Google.

items.title: The internet needs a nap (and you do, too)
items.summary: Bill urges prioritizing environmental awareness and team stability over reactive patching, suggesting the internet and teams need a break.

items.title: Nvidia adds possible hack to list of very bad things under investigation
items.summary: Nvidia is investigating a potential hack linked to a ransomware group that has set a deadline for the company to pay a ransom or risk its data being leaked.

items.title: NGINX2Root: F5 patches five critical NGINX vulnerabilities
items.summary: F5 has released patches for five critical vulnerabilities in NGINX that could allow remote code execution. The issues, identified as NGINX2Root, were also reported by multiple security researchers.

items.title: Transport for London breach exposes 265,000 Oyster card users' data
items.summary: Transport for London disclosed that personal details of approximately 265,000 Oyster card customers may have been exposed in a data breach.

items.title: DOJ, DHS partner on new unit tackling scams and cybercrime
items.summary: The Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security have launched the Threat Disruption Center to improve triage of victim complaints, map cybercriminal networks, and provide a direct channel to private sector partners.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Dems call CISA nominee ‘disqualified’ after nomination hearing
items.summary: Democratic members of the committee criticized CISA nominee Michael LoSapio during the nomination hearing, labeling him as disqualified after disputes over election and January 6 matters.

items.title: Cold Relic: What you need to know
items.summary: Cold Relic, a Russian espionage group formerly known as COLDRIVER, is known for infiltrating organizations by impersonating trusted individuals.

items.title: CISA nominee LoSapio vows to bolster cyber defenses while denying Jan. 6 Capitol attack
items.summary: CISA nominee Michael LoSapio pledged to strengthen the agency's cyber defenses and denied any involvement in the January 6 Capitol attack during his testimony.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
items.summary: The phpAfterShell vulnerability allows attackers to manipulate PHP session storage to inject objects that can lead to remote code execution. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-126714, has been fixed in current PHP releases.

items.title: PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs
items.summary: PHP released security updates that address 18 vulnerabilities, including critical bugs that could enable unauthenticated remote code execution on vulnerable servers.

items.title: Russian national accused of stalking San Francisco techie in plot against US defense-tech giant
items.summary: The Department of Justice accuses a Russian national of stalking a San Francisco technology employee as part of a four‑month operation to steal secrets and surveil employees of a U.S. defense‑tech company.

items.title: UK court confirms British government served Apple with secret encryption notice
items.summary: UK tribunal confirms the British government served Apple with a secret legal notice targeting iCloud encryption, ending two years of denial.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: PHP Patches Seven Critical RCE Vulnerabilities
items.summary: PHP has released patches for seven critical remote code execution vulnerabilities that could crash worker processes and allow code execution with worker privileges.

items.title: CyberPower PowerPanel Exploited to Run Malicious Code on Domain Controller
items.summary: Symantec discovered attackers used CyberPower UPS software to run malicious scripts on a domain controller, enabling code execution.

items.title: PHP 8.6 is out, and here’s what changes for your code
items.summary: PHP 8.6 introduces partial function application, a Time\Duration class, a polling API for event loops, and a clamp() function. It also changes session defaults to enable strict mode, HTTP-only cookies, and Lax same-site policy, requiring custom handlers to implement both creation and destruction methods.

items.title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaw (CVSS 9.8) Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
items.summary: A critical VMware vCenter vulnerability (CVSS 9.8) allows network attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access. Fixed versions are available for all supported branches, and no workaround is provided.

items.title: Spying on Governments with Zero Lines of Malware: A Custom SoftEther Bridge in Webworm’s Toolkit
items.summary: Webworm, a China‑aligned APT, deploys the open‑source SoftEther VPN to infiltrate government networks, providing low‑profile, long‑term access.

items.title: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
items.summary: Ransomware attacks often begin with credential theft, lateral movement, and disabling security controls before encryption. Acronis identifies five warning signs to help defenders detect and contain intrusions early.

items.title: Critical NGINX ‘NGINX2Root’ bugs let attackers hijack servers
items.summary: Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities, dubbed "nginx2root", enable unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely. Researchers demonstrated chaining these flaws with a Linux kernel bug to achieve root access.

items.title: PHP Fixes 7 Critical Flaws, Including Bugs That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
items.summary: The PHP Foundation released security updates addressing seven critical flaws that could lead to remote code execution, including CVE-2026-115560 with a CVSS score of 9.2.

items.title: Russian spies turn one cloud breach into a stepping stone for the next
items.summary: A Russian cyberespionage group, known as COLD RELIC, impersonates employees of previously breached organizations to phish new targets, focusing on government, defense, and critical infrastructure.

items.title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw That Could Give Unauthenticated Attackers Control of Sites
items.summary: Drupal core contains a critical installer flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers use the installer to reinstall a site, potentially leading to takeover or remote code execution. Fixed releases are available for all supported branches.

items.title: Nvidia Responds to Gentlemen Ransomware Claim
items.summary: Nvidia stated it found no evidence of compromise after the Gentlemen ransomware group listed the company as a victim.

items.title: Why Holiday Security Can't Wait for Black Friday
items.summary: Bot-driven fraud and holiday social engineering attacks extend across many weeks, straining security teams and small businesses during the holiday season.

items.title: Ukraine exposes ransomware network extorting US oil, healthcare firms
items.summary: Ukrainian authorities arrested four suspects linked to an international ransomware network that extorted more than $40 million from U.S. oil and healthcare firms.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Hackers Exploit Cisco Expressway Vulnerability Soon After PoC Release
items.summary: Hackers exploited a Cisco Expressway vulnerability shortly after a proof‑of‑concept was released. They targeted clustered devices at a Russian organization and prepared tooling for lateral movement.

items.title: Drupal patches critical RCE flaw, warns exploits may surface quickly
items.summary: Drupal patched a critical remote code execution flaw that could allow attackers to take over vulnerable sites. The security team warned that exploits may surface quickly.

items.title: Exploited Puppet flaw puts the server that configures your endpoint fleet at risk (CVE-2026-115731)
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑115731, a critical RCE in Perforce Puppet Enterprise, is being exploited in the wild. The US CISA has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list.

items.title: StepSecurity Secures $20 Million to Expand Supply Chain Protection
items.summary: StepSecurity raised $20 million to expand its supply‑chain protection platform. The funding will accelerate development and distribution of its security solutions.

items.title: Critical Apache Roller, Axis Vulnerabilities Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: Attackers are exploiting critical Apache Roller and Axis vulnerabilities. Confluence Data Center is targeted via an Axis flaw, while Apache warns of attacks against Roller.

items.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks confirmed attackers exploited two PHP vulnerabilities (CVE‑2026‑109618 and CVE‑2026‑109619) against PAN‑OS management interfaces. The flaws allow unauthenticated code execution.

items.title: Microsoft tests new Edge Lockdown Mode that disables GPU APIs
items.summary: Microsoft is testing a new Edge Lockdown Mode that disables WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU APIs to reduce the browser’s attack surface.

items.title: Cyberattack on service provider exposes payee data at 40 Irish credit unions
items.summary: A cyberattack on Wellington IT exposed payee data at 40 Irish credit unions. The minister called the notification delay "not acceptable."

items.title: TfL Warns 265,000 Photocard Customers May Have Had Personal Data Exposed
items.summary: TfL warned that 265,000 Oyster Photocard customers may have had personal data exposed after emails were sent from its system.

items.title: BackBox Linux 10 brings new hacking tools and Ubuntu 26.04 support
items.summary: BackBox Linux 10, codenamed Resolute Raccoon, was released with new hacking tools and support for Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. It ships with Linux 7.0 kernel, Xfce 4.20 desktop, and updated anonymous mode.

items.title: TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline after attackers compromise customer accounts
items.summary: TfL shut down the Oyster photocard website after attackers accessed approximately 265,000 customer accounts. The service remains offline pending a security fix.

items.title: Rubrik Configuration Resilience rolls back unauthorized Microsoft 365 changes
items.summary: Rubrik introduced Configuration Resilience for Microsoft 365, allowing a single action to roll back unauthorized changes to key Microsoft settings and continuously protect configurations.

items.title: SonicWall urges customers to replace Gen 6 firewalls now
items.summary: SonicWall urged customers to replace Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 firewalls immediately, as SonicOS 6.x has reached end of support and will no longer receive firmware updates or patches.

items.title: Splunk Patches Nearly 140 Flaws Across Three Core Products
items.summary: Splunk released updates for three core products, fixing nearly 140 critical and high‑severity vulnerabilities that could enable authentication bypass, remote code execution, and privilege escalation.

items.title: Bitwarden expands passkey support with new Windows and macOS integrations
items.summary: Bitwarden added passkey integration for Windows Hello and Apple Touch ID, enabling users to unlock their vaults via native OS authentication on Windows 11 and macOS.

items.title: Microsoft confirms app installation, launch issues after hotpatch
items.summary: Microsoft provided a workaround for installation and launch issues affecting Office and third‑party applications caused by the latest Windows 11 hotpatch.

items.title: F5 Patches Critical NGINX2Root Flaws as PoC Exploits Go Public
items.summary: F5 Networks patched five NGINX2Root vulnerabilities that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution; proof‑of‑concept exploits were publicly released.

items.title: Sticky note on monitor provided keys to the company’s kingdom
items.summary: A sticky note left on a monitor exposed company credentials, demonstrating the risk of leaving sensitive information in public view.

items.title: GTA 6 scams are after your Google password, money, and crypto wallet
items.summary: Scammers targeting the GTA 6 launch are phishing for Google passwords, selling fake game keys, and requesting crypto wallet connections to steal funds.

items.title: Hackers Breach N-able Cloud Server, Disrupting Email Security Management Across 3 Regions
items.summary: N‑able disclosed that attackers accessed a server in its Mail Assure and Spam Experts hosted cloud, disabling management interfaces and APIs across three regions; the company is mitigating the threat and hardening services.

items.title: NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims
items.summary: NVIDIA is investigating claims that the Gentlemen ransomware group has listed the company on a dark‑web data‑leak site. The investigation follows reports of a potential security breach. No further details have been released.

items.title: Rakuten Securities Breach Could Impact 15 Million Customers
items.summary: Japanese broker Rakuten Securities disclosed a data breach that exposed account details of 15 million customers. The breach could affect a large portion of the company's client base. No additional information has been provided.

items.title: Java4Shell Exploitation Attempts Begin as Vendors Rush Out Advisories
items.summary: Multiple vendors released advisories on the Java4Shell vulnerability. GreyNoise, WatchTowr, and Cloudflare reported probing and exploit attempts. Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, and Siemens detailed the impact of the flaw.

items.title: Ruby Releases Fixes for 7 Regex and String Flaws, Warns 5 Have Proof-of-Concept RCE
items.summary: Ruby released patches for seven memory‑safety flaws in its regex engine and string conversion code. Maintainers warned that five of these flaws have proof‑of‑concept remote code execution exploits. The fixes are now available.

items.title: Researcher Demonstrates Database RCE Exploits Affecting PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
items.summary: A researcher demonstrated that low‑privilege database accounts can trigger code execution on PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, and Oracle. The exploits exploit memory‑corruption bugs in the database engines. Proof‑of‑concepts were published.

items.title: CISA Warns of 4 Exploited Flaws Linked to Ransomware, Cryptomining, and LLMjacking Attacks
items.summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaws affect Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and REDCap. Evidence of active exploitation was cited.

items.title: Africa Retakes Top Spot as Most Attacked Region, Led by Nigeria Surge
items.summary: Africa reclaimed the top spot as the most attacked region, driven by a surge in cyber threats in Nigeria. Angola and Kenya also ranked in the top five most‑attacked countries worldwide. The trend reflects a growing regional threat landscape.

items.title: My IoT devices are no longer supported – is my smart home safe?
items.summary: End‑of‑life smart devices pose security risks if unmanaged; users should secure or replace them to protect their smart homes.

items.title: PHP Readies Critical Security Updates to Patch Another RCE Flaw
items.summary: PHP announced critical security updates to patch CVE‑2026‑115560, which affected session upload progress. The release follows the PHP2Shell patches. The update addresses a remote code execution flaw.

items.title: PHP Warns of Critical Security Flaws Affecting All Supported Versions, Fixes Coming November 19
items.summary: PHP maintainers issued an advisory for an upcoming release on November 19, 2026, that will address critical vulnerabilities across all supported versions. The release is scheduled between 2:00 and 2:30 p.m. UTC. The update follows the regular four‑week release cycle.

items.title: Russian charged with spying on Palantir employees for Moscow
items.summary: A Russian national, Igor Andreevich D’iu, was charged in the United States with acting as a Moscow agent spying on employees of Palantir Technologies. The individual was recruited through Telegram. The charges relate to a surveillance campaign targeting Palantir staff.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Ransomware access brokers are moving their deals off public forums
items.summary: Ransomware and extortion gangs claimed about 718 victims per month in October 2026, up from roughly 573 in 2025. Public dark‑web listings for hacked network access fell from about 620 to 370 per quarter, indicating brokers are moving deals off public forums.

items.title: Ukraine, FBI arrest ransomware gang members tied to $40M in ransoms
items.summary: Ukrainian authorities and the FBI arrested four suspects from an international ransomware group linked to more than $40.5 million in ransom payments from at least 28 companies worldwide.

items.title: Azure Linux 4 puts the OS behind Microsoft’s cloud services on your VMs at no extra license fee
items.summary: Microsoft released Azure Linux 4 as a general‑purpose server OS for virtual machines and scale sets. The distribution is available at no additional license fee; customers pay only for Azure compute resources.

items.title: Get ready for another critical PHP security release to drop
items.summary: A critical remote‑code‑execution vulnerability in PHP will be addressed in an upcoming security release scheduled for Thursday.

items.title: Russia's Cold Relic APT Turns One Cloud Breach Into Another
items.summary: The Russia‑linked threat group Cold Relic uses data stolen from one victim to target others through convincing impersonations and social‑engineering attacks.

items.title: AttackIQ Research Reveals How Iranian Cyber Groups Hand Off Network Access to Enable Destructive Attacks
items.summary: AttackIQ research of 20 Iranian state‑sponsored groups shows how they hand off network access to enable espionage, ransomware, and hacktivism in state‑backed campaigns.

items.title: Trump administration officials size-up a bad stretch for tech
items.summary: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the administration will reach out to industry to share information about major patches before they take effect.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Data breach impacts 40 Irish credit unions in reported IT provider hack
items.summary: A cyberattack on Wellington IT exposed sensitive data belonging to members of 50 credit unions, most of which are located in Ireland.

items.title: Senate Republicans advance FCC nominee, slate of cyber bills
items.summary: Senate Republicans advanced an FCC nominee, giving them a 3‑1 majority, while multiple bipartisan cyber bills remain in limbo after Democrats missed the markup hearing.

items.title: It’s NGINX’s turn to cause vulnpocalypse headaches
items.summary: Researchers released five NGINX exploits, including one that chains an HTTP/2 bug with a kernel flaw to seize control of the underlying machine.

items.title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
items.summary: NGINX’s HTTP/2 flaw (CVE‑2026‑123007) allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled. The vulnerability has existed since 2015 and is fixed in NGINX 1.31.9 and 1.30.7.

items.title: F5 Warns 6 Critical BIG-IP Flaws Can Crash Traffic in Specific Setups, May Allow RCE
items.summary: F5 disclosed six critical BIG‑IP vulnerabilities that can crash the Traffic Management Microkernel without authentication and may enable remote code execution in specific virtual‑server configurations.

items.title: California tells Waymo to take the next exit after freeway mishaps
items.summary: California regulators ordered Waymo to suspend driverless rides on high‑speed roads nationwide after construction‑zone incidents and a collision with patrol vehicles.

items.title: Microsoft's official Python agent framework hijacked to distribute malware
items.summary: An attacker compromised Microsoft’s official Python Agent Framework GitHub organization admin credentials, enabling the distribution of malware through the framework.

items.title: Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required
items.summary: Apache Roller’s XML‑RPC endpoint (CVE‑2026‑129448) is actively exploited, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution via deserialization of untrusted XML data.

items.title: Microsoft’s Agent Framework PyPI package compromised to steal credentials
items.summary: Hackers released malicious versions of Microsoft’s Agent Framework Python package on PyPI that harvest cloud credentials and other sensitive information from developers’ systems.

items.title: Five Critical Vulnerabilities Found in World's Most Widely Used Open-Source Web Server
items.summary: Five critical NGINX vulnerabilities enable unauthenticated remote code execution, potentially giving attackers full control over affected servers.

items.title: NSA continues response to interruptions in classified internal network
items.summary: The NSA reports ongoing disruptions to its classified internal network, with staggered logins and arrivals at Fort Meade, but national‑security work continues uninterrupted.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Cyber insurers now want proof you can actually recover
items.summary: Insurance carriers now require evidence of successful data recovery, not just a green backup status, as part of tighter underwriting for cyber insurance.

items.title: Russian cyber-espionage group used stolen cloud data to hack into organizations, Google says
items.summary: Google research indicates Russian state‑backed hackers used stolen cloud account data to impersonate contacts and launch espionage attacks against victims’ professional networks.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: CVE-2026-123007: Critical NGINX HTTP/2 Integer Underflow Leads to RCE (FIXED)
items.summary: CVE-2026-123007 is a critical integer underflow in NGINX HTTP/2 that can lead to unauthenticated remote code execution. Rapid7 and F5 have released a patch. The vulnerability is rated CVSS 9.2.

items.title: Who was that trying to phone me just now? How one-ring phone scams work
items.summary: One-ring phone scams, known as 'wangiri', lure victims after a single ring. The article explains how to recognize and avoid these scams.

items.title: Product showcase: iVerify Basic helps users check device security and improve privacy
items.summary: iVerify Basic is a mobile app for iOS and Android that scans devices for compromise indicators and displays security status. It offers a single-screen interface for running scans and reviewing findings. The app is free for individual users.

items.title: Fraudsters feed the right face into identity checks through virtual cameras
items.summary: Fraudsters use virtual cameras to feed manipulated facial images into identity verification systems. The technique is part of a broader trend of document fraud, which remains the largest attack category. Medium‑sophistication attacks account for nearly 39% of cases.

items.title: Oracle reveals fix-this-ASAP-grade Java4Shell bug that allows attacks on many third-party apps
items.summary: Oracle has issued a critical patch for the Java4Shell vulnerability that can crash the JVM or enable unauthenticated remote code execution. The flaw affects many third‑party Java applications. Users should update to the latest Java release immediately.

items.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
items.summary: A vulnerability in Optimizely’s A/B testing platform allowed attackers to inject malware into at least 178 high‑traffic websites. The malicious code targeted visitors with data‑stealing exploits. The incident involved sites such as BBC, CNN, and Equifax.

items.title: CVE-2026-114938: Critical vulnerability in OpenJDK Java
items.summary: CVE-2026-114938, also known as Java4Shell, is a critical flaw in OpenJDK that permits unauthenticated remote code execution. Cisco Talos reports a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2. A patch is available for affected Java versions.
